scientific_rationale: The Analyst selected the single native_rms_ratio intervention on L109 and framed the choice as prospective between 0.165 and 0.66. Both variants are legal local_nc_layout patches with identical structure: same atom_slots, typed_slots [12,22], typed_elements [C,N], same anchor (A:VAL:116:N at slot 22, strength 0.951), same window [0.1,0.5], same steps, same native_options, and the same weights {half:1.0, endpoint:0.0, orientation:0.0, type:0.0}. The only difference is dose.native_rms_ratio (0.165 vs 0.66). Because orientation weight is zero, the anchor is inactive and no orientation term is enabled; the only enabled positive-weight term is half. The R01 calibration realization shows the native C12/N22 layout is not fragile to native-RMS perturbation: boundary probabilities were already high (C 0.9427, N 0.9479), joint_formation was 0.25, and retention_after_formation was 1.0, so the native suffix survived to the final state. The retention_prior diagnostic (24 extra attempts, not independent seeds) shows low retention among boundary-correct slots (N 0.077, C 0.154) and joint layout correct-at-final-same-slots 1/24, indicating the binding constraint is not native-RMS dose but the typed final output, which did not change (final_prediction_changed_typed_fraction 0.0). Since no native_rms_ratio dose has actually been tested (R01 chosen_value null), the higher dose 0.66 is the discriminating direction: it is the larger perturbation that can test whether the unchanged typed output can be moved, while the measured retention insensitivity argues against the lower dose 0.165 being justified by retention risk. The source layout_score 8.704859 is not a generated score forecast; parent generated scores are mean 7.6826 and best_qualified 8.3780.
